change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration aborts on any install where embed_category was never set
findings.body: The first query joins site_settings.embed_category to categories.name and then calls `[0]['id']` on the result. Whenever embed_category is unset or blank (its default is '' in the base config/site_settings.yml, and no category has an empty name), the result has zero rows, `[0]` is nil or raises, and the migration stops before copying any host. Every site that never configured embedding would fail `db:migrate`. Line 15 has the same shape: `[0]['value']` on the uncategorized_category_id query. Fix: check for a row before reading it (e.g. take the first row only if one exists) and fall back to the uncategorized id when there is none.
findings.originReason: The migration is new in this diff.

verification.reason: Site settings that were never changed have no row in site_settings (embed_category's default '' lives in the yml), so the JOIN returns zero rows and `[0]['id']` fails on the PG::Result: IndexError, or nil['id']. Any install that never set embed_category therefore aborts db:migrate.

findings.title: Migrated host entries are copied raw and skip validation, so existing embeds break silently
findings.body: Each line of the old embeddable_hosts setting is inserted as-is. The old check (allows_embeddable_host?, removed in app/models/site_setting.rb by this PR) stripped a leading http:// or https://, so existing installs may hold entries like 'http://example.com'. The new lookup compares lower(host) with the referer's bare host (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14-17), so those entries never match and embedding stops after upgrade with no error shown to the admin. Entries that fail the model regex (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2, TLD of 2-5 letters) are inserted too, and then cannot be saved again from the admin UI. Blank lines and CR characters become rows with empty or '\r' hosts, and a quote in an entry breaks the SQL. Fix: normalise each entry the same way before_validation does (trim, strip scheme and path, skip blanks) and bind values instead of interpolating them.
findings.originReason: The migration and the new lookup are both added in this diff.

verification.reason: The old check stripped http(s):// from each stored entry before comparing. The migration copies entries as they are, and record_for_host compares lower(host) with the bare uri.host, so entries like 'http://x.com' stop matching. The values are also interpolated into the SQL with no trimming and no skipping of blank lines.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts are accepted; the oldest silently wins
findings.body: Validation only checks format (lines 2-3), and the migration creates no unique index. The admin can add the same host twice with different categories. `where(...).first` has no explicit order, so Rails orders by primary key and the oldest row always wins. The second category is never used and nothing tells the admin. Fix: validate host uniqueness (case-insensitive) in the model, and optionally add a unique index.
findings.originReason: The model is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The model only validates format and the migration creates no unique index, so duplicate hosts can be saved. `where(...).first` then returns the row with the lowest id, and the other category is never used.

findings.title: 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes without testing hosts
findings.body: No embeddable host is created in this example. The result is false anyway, because embed_truncate defaults to false and the Fabricate.build topic has no topic_embed, so has_topic_embed? is false. The example would pass whether or not any host gate exists. The describe at line 1407 also has a typo ('emeddable'). Rewrite the example to test the behaviour it names, or rename it to match what the code now does (see the expandable_first_post? finding).
findings.originReason: This diff rewrote the example and removed the host check from expandable_first_post?.

verification.reason: expandable_first_post? no longer looks at hosts at all. The example returns false only because embed_truncate defaults to false and an unsaved topic has no TopicEmbed, so it would pass whether or not any host exists.

findings.title: 'find embedded' asks for fruit 2 but the mock always returns fruit 1
findings.body: `store.find('fruit', 2)` is called, but the `/fruits/:id` handler in test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:226-229 ignores the id and returns fruits[0] (apple). The assertions on colors [1, 2] are apple's colors, not banana's (id 2, color_ids [3]), so the test does not check that the requested record is returned. Make the mock look up request.params.id, or request fruit 1.
findings.originReason: This diff changed the requested id from 1 to 2 and added the color assertions.

verification.reason: The /fruits/:id handler always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]). The test asks for fruit 2 (banana, color_ids [3]) but asserts apple's colors, so it never checks that the requested record comes back.

findings.title: Failed delete gives no feedback
findings.body: `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no catch, so a failed DELETE leaves the row in place with no message and an unhandled rejection. The save action uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`; delete should too.
findings.originReason: The component is new in this diff.

verification.reason: destroyRecord().then(...) has no catch, so a failed DELETE gives the admin no feedback. save() uses .catch(popupAjaxError).

findings.title: update, destroy and create raise 500 on a missing record or missing params
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first` returns nil when another admin has just deleted the host. Then `nil.destroy` (line 16) or `save_host(nil)` (line 11, then `nil.host=` at line 23) raises NoMethodError and returns 500. A request without an `embeddable_host` key fails the same way at line 23. Use find (404) or check for nil and return a JSON error.
findings.originReason: The controller is new in this diff.

verification.reason: where(...).first returns nil for a missing id, and both host.destroy and host.host= then raise NoMethodError. A request without the embeddable_host param fails the same way, at params[:embeddable_host][:host].

findings.title: before_validation raises if host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, for example when a create or update request omits the host key. The error surfaces as a 500 rather than a 422 validation error. Guard with `if host`, or use `host.to_s`.
findings.originReason: The model is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard. The controller assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which is nil when the key is missing, so validation raises NoMethodError instead of adding an error.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns success and saves nothing
findings.body: `update` renders the unchanged serializer and persists nothing, and config/routes.rb:139 exposes it. Nothing in the UI reaches it: embedding.hbs has no save control, so `saveChanges` in app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7 is dead code. Remove the route, the action and saveChanges, or make the action do what it claims.
findings.originReason: The controller and the route are new in this diff.

verification.reason: update renders the serializer without saving anything, config/routes.rb:139 exposes it, and nothing calls the controller's saveChanges action: embedding.hbs only has the addHost button.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer requires any embeddable host
findings.body: Removing `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` means an embedded topic with embed_truncate on is expandable even on a site with no embed hosts. Before this PR it returned false in that case. Is that intended? If so, the spec at spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1403 needs changing. If not, restore a host check.
findings.originReason: The host check was removed by this diff.

verification.reason: The diff removes the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` check and adds no host check in its place, so the method now depends only on embed_truncate and has_topic_embed?.

findings.title: Imports from unlisted hosts lose the configured embed category
findings.body: Before, every imported topic used SiteSetting.embed_category. Now only URLs whose host is in the list get a category. For any other URL, eh is nil and lib/topic_creator.rb:100 sets no category_id, so the topic is uncategorized. Import paths that do not check the host list (feed polling, Jobs::PollFeed, not read) would therefore change behaviour. Is that intended? spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only covers a listed host, so this case is untested.
findings.originReason: This diff replaced SiteSetting.embed_category with the per-host lookup.

verification.reason: Jobs::PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import with no host check. If the feed URL's host has no EmbeddableHost row, eh is nil, the category is nil, and TopicCreator sets no category_id. Before, embed_category was always used.

findings.title: Every *_ids array in rest-serialized responses is now rewritten
findings.body: The regex now matches plural keys for all responses with __rest_serializer. If an id has no sideloaded object, _lookupSubType returns undefined (lines 157-187), so the array gets undefined entries and the raw key is deleted. `hydrated || []` on line 200 can never fall back, since map always returns an array. Today only the embedding response carries an id array (the other rest responses use has_one), so this is latent. Filter out unresolved ids and keep the raw key when nothing resolves.
findings.originReason: This diff added the plural _ids branch.

verification.reason: _lookupSubType falls through and returns undefined when the id is missing from the collection. The map then keeps undefined entries, the raw key is always deleted, and `hydrated || []` can never fall back because map always returns an array.

findings.title: Fabricator contents are swapped between the two files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now holds the embeddable_host fabricator, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators. Swap them back so each file has the name of its contents.
findings.originReason: This diff replaced the contents of category_fabricator.rb.

verification.reason: category_fabricator.rb now defines only :embeddable_host, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the :category fabricators.

findings.title: Admin host controller specs only check inheritance
findings.body: The spec asserts only that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController. It does not exercise create, update or destroy, the 422 path or the missing-record path. spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7 has the same gap for show and update.
findings.originReason: The spec is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The only example asserts the class hierarchy; no action is exercised.

findings.title: admin.embedding.edit is never used
findings.body: No template or JS in app/ references admin.embedding.edit. Remove it.

verification.reason: Searching app/ finds admin.embedding.host, category, add_host, title and confirm_delete, but nothing uses admin.embedding.edit. The edit button is icon-only.

findings.title: Migration cannot be rolled back, and the old settings are gone
findings.body: The migration is a `change` method that contains raw execute calls, and it deletes the old site settings on line 31. Rails cannot reverse raw SQL, so rolling it back should raise IrreversibleMigration, and the old settings cannot be restored from the migration. Write explicit up and down methods, or document that rollback is unsupported.
findings.originReason: The migration is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The migration uses `change` with raw execute calls, including the DELETE of the old settings, and has no up/down or reversible block. A rollback cannot invert execute, and nothing restores the deleted settings.

contracts.action: Open the Embedding admin page (route model load)
contracts.before_after: Before: no page. After: store.find('embedding') GETs /admin/customize/embedding via the embedding adapter, and the result is hydrated from result.embedding.
contracts.visible_effect: A table of hosts, or only the Add Host button when the list is empty.
contracts.failure_mode: The route has no error handler, so a rejected find is not caught in this part.

contracts.before_after: Creates an unsaved record with no id and pushes it onto embedding.embeddable_hosts. Nothing is written to the store map, because storeMap ignores records without an id.
contracts.visible_effect: A new row opens in edit mode, since the component's editing flag is host.isNew.
contracts.failure_mode: Cancel removes the unsaved row. Leaving the page discards it, because nothing persists it.

contracts.action: Save host (create or update from the row)
contracts.before_after: Before: the row is in edit mode. After: save posts or puts through the REST adapter to /admin/embeddable_hosts(/:id), then the row returns to read mode and host.category is set from the category cache.
contracts.visible_effect: The row shows the saved values. A server 422 goes to popupAjaxError.
contracts.failure_mode: popupAjaxError runs on rejection, so the failure is visible. isSaving is reset in finally (rest.js.es6 model lines 29 and 55).
contracts.open_question: If the user leaves the page while a save is in flight, the promise's then-callback calls this.set on a destroyed component. Ember may assert or warn there, and the .catch would then show a popup. This depends on Ember's destroyed-object behaviour, which I did not read.

contracts.before_after: Before: the row exists. After: DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id, then sendAction removes the row from the controller's list.
contracts.failure_mode: There is no catch on destroyRecord().then, so a failed DELETE leaves the row with no message and an unhandled rejection.

contracts.before_after: A new row is removed through deleteHost. An existing row has its buffer discarded and editToggled reset.
contracts.visible_effect: The row returns to read mode, or disappears if it was new.
contracts.failure_mode: None: there is no async call here.

contracts.before_after: Before: no such action. After: loads by id, destroys, returns success json.
contracts.visible_effect: Success json, and the client removes the row.
contracts.failure_mode: If the id is missing, nil.destroy raises NoMethodError and the response is a 500 (line 16). The record is re-fetched by id in the same request, so no stale-target check is needed.

contracts.before_after: Before: none. After: assigns host and category_id (blank becomes uncategorized), saves, and renders the serializer or a 422 error.
contracts.visible_effect: Saved row, or the validation error popup.
contracts.failure_mode: An unknown id gives nil at line 11, then NoMethodError at line 23. A missing params[:embeddable_host] also raises. A nil host in the model raises in before_validation.

contracts.before_after: Before: no route. After: the route is accepted, nothing is written, and the serialized data is returned.
contracts.visible_effect: None. Nothing in the UI calls it: embedding.hbs has no save control.
contracts.failure_mode: Not applicable, because nothing persists. The endpoint reports success while changing nothing.

contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/site_setting.rb:68-72 (base commit: SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?, removed by this PR)
contracts.before_after: Before: a blank list raised, then allows_embeddable_host? compared the referer host with a list. After: one EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? call (case-insensitive DB lookup, one query per request).
contracts.visible_effect: Embed page error for a disallowed referer.
contracts.failure_mode: A nil referer makes URI(nil) raise, which record_for_host rescues to nil, so the request is refused. Consistent with the old behaviour.

contracts.before_after: Before: the category came from SiteSetting.embed_category, a name looked up by find_category. After: the category_id of the host matching the URL, or nil for an unlisted host.
contracts.visible_effect: The topic's category. An unlisted host now gets no category, which before happened only when embed_category was blank.
contracts.failure_mode: nil skips category_id, so the topic is uncategorized. This is the same outcome as the old blank-setting case.
contracts.open_question: Import paths that do not check the host list, such as feed polling, would now lose the configured category. Jobs::PollFeed was not read.

contracts.before_after: Before: required SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?, embed_truncate and has_topic_embed?. After: embed_truncate and has_topic_embed? only.
contracts.visible_effect: Embedded topics are expandable even with no hosts configured.
Same retrieve gating, now from the table.
contracts.failure_mode: A false result skips the retrieve, as before.

contracts.before_after: Before: only singular _id keys were hydrated. After: plural _ids keys become an array under the plural name and the raw key is deleted, even when entries do not resolve.
contracts.visible_effect: The embedding table rows. Unresolved entries would show as blank rows.
contracts.failure_mode: _lookupSubType returns undefined for an id not in the root (store.js:157-187), so the array holds undefined entries. The embedding response sideloads hosts (application_serializer.rb:2 embed :ids, include: true), so today this resolves.

contracts.action: Destructive migration step: DELETE of old site settings and INSERT of hosts
contracts.before_after: Before: the old settings existed. After: each host from the setting is inserted, then the rows are deleted.
contracts.visible_effect: The embedding hosts table is populated and the old settings are gone.
contracts.failure_mode: Target check: the DELETE targets exactly the two named setting rows, and it runs only after the insert loop; an exception skips it. Inserts are not checked, and raw values are copied (see finding on line 25). Rollback is not possible (see finding on line 31).

contracts.before_after: Before: exact membership test. After: membership test after replacing the first underscore with a dash. For the existing dash-named types the result is the same.
contracts.visible_effect: None for existing callers: admin-customize-css-html.js.es6:6,16 and admin-plugins.js.es6:3 use dash names.

summary: Reviewed all 37 files of part 1. The main blocker is the migration: its first query reads `[0]['id']` from a join that returns zero rows whenever `embed_category` is unset, which is the default, so `db:migrate` aborts for every site that never configured embedding. Other findings: migrated host entries are copied raw (http:// prefixes and entries that fail the model regex stop working or cannot be re-saved), duplicate hosts are accepted with the oldest silently winning, one spec passes without testing hosts, and the store test requests fruit 2 from a mock that always returns fruit 1. Smaller items cover missing-record 500s, a no-op PUT endpoint, a removed host gate in expandable_first_post?, and cleanup. No ADRs exist in docs/adr, and no remaining callers of the removed settings or helpers were found in app/ or lib/.
